proof:
Source: the change of variables x = R₀y of step B1 of the parent proof, isolated with r in place of R₀. Fix n, F and r > 0, and write B_ρ := ball (0 : Euclid n) ρ.
1. (Balls.) r·B_1 = B_r (smul_unitBall_of_pos; pointwise scalar action on sets, open scoped Pointwise). Moreover, for every y, r·y ∈ B_r if and only if y ∈ B_1, because ‖r·y‖ = r‖y‖ and r > 0.
2. (Dimension and measure.) finrank ℝ (Euclid n) = n (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin), and Lebesgue measure on Euclid n is an additive Haar measure.
3. (Integral identity.) Measure.setIntegral_comp_smul_of_pos (Haar measure volume, function F, set B_1, r > 0) states ∫_{B_1} F(r·y) dy = (r^{finrank ℝ (Euclid n)})⁻¹ • ∫_{r·B_1} F(x) dx, and it holds for every F because non-integrable functions have integral 0 on both sides. By steps 1–2 the right side equals r^{−n}·∫_{B_r} F(x) dx.
4. (Integrability.) For a measurable set s, a function is integrable on s if and only if its indicator function on s is integrable on ℝⁿ (integrable_indicator_iff; balls are measurable). By step 1, for every y, the indicator of y ↦ F(r·y) on B_1, evaluated at y, equals H(r·y), where H is the indicator of F on B_r (both equal F(r·y) if y ∈ B_1 and 0 otherwise). By integrable_comp_smul_iff (Haar measure, r ≠ 0), y ↦ H(r·y) is integrable if and only if H is integrable. Chaining these equivalences: y ↦ F(r·y) is integrable on B_1 if and only if F is integrable on B_r. ∎
key_steps: Measure.setIntegral_comp_smul_of_pos with finrank ℝ (Euclid n) = n gives the integral identity for every F.
Integrability: pass to indicator functions and use integrable_comp_smul_iff.
